500 years have passed since the tumultuous events of **The Chaotic Era I: The Gods of Reason**, a decisive chapter in history. It all began during the Theoclasm, a cataclysmic event triggered when the Theoclasts, a technologically advanced race, captured the powerful deity YHVH, resulting in the devastation of the old continent of Pectus. Fleeing the horrors of this apocalypse, the survivors sought refuge on the distant shores of Yuandi, where the saga of **The Chaotic Era II: The New Mythology** will take place.
**Theoclasm:**
The term "Theoclasm", derived from *Théos* (God, Deity, Divinity) and *Klastós* (Broken, Fractured), encapsulates the pivotal moment that incited the mass exodus from Pectus. YHVH, the god of light and ruler of Paradise, fell into the clutches of the Theoclasts, leading to the apotheosis of Ptah-Khnemu. Strengthened by this deity, the Theoclasts became an unstoppable force, leading Ma'at, who later allied himself with mortals, to reveal that Ptah-Khnemu imagined a world free from the control of the deities, but was still undecided whether to exterminate the mortals who disagreed with his vision or allying with supporters. A betrayal unfolded when Montu-Sekhmet, daughter of Ptah-Khnemu himself, seized power during the height of Theoclasm, having intentions contrary to those of her father, seeking to rebuild the universe from scratch.
Ma'at, who millennia ago was infused with a deity whose name was lost to time, escaped the clutches of her own race, seeking refuge in Yuandi lest she become a mere tool or source of power. With her advanced technological knowledge and divine abilities, she erected five monumental pillars, enclosing the new continent within a protective barrier. This sanctuary attracted not only mortal inhabitants but also lesser deities, fearful of a Theoclast incursion. After Ma'at's death, her essence fragmented, each fragment containing a portion of her memories and powers, while her remains were buried in the reliquary of the Archbishopric of Ma'at, where she is believed to still work miracles.
After the fall of YHVH, the angels, previously subservient to the deity, regained their free will, while the demons were thrown into disarray following the disappearance of their master. The ensuing chaos led to an anarchic exodus from Hell, the domain of their lord ALMF (Alumniferus), resulting in confusion and insanity, which led to the suicide of many angels and demons. Some remaining demons now disguise themselves as mortals and mythical beings from Yuandi. Although many angels strive to defend YHVH's legacy through their temples, the whereabouts of the goddess of chaos, NLTP (Niarlatotepe), and the god of darkness remain unknown within the protective barrier.
These turbulent consequences and the unstable balance of divine forces now set the stage for an epic story of survival, power struggles, and ever-shifting alliances within Yuandi.
Now for the races' lore:

Renshi
The Rénshi are one of the native races of the new continent and are the most numerous race. Most inhabit the Ozumi Empire (based on the Empire of Japan), with significant numbers in the Wildlands, the territory of the Followers of Ma'at, and the southern tip of Igirith. The Shun culture, named after the eponymous Shun Dynasty (based on Chinese culture), once almost dominated the entire continent, making them enemies of other races and cultures. The Ozumi Empire, originating from the outlying islands east of the Shun lands, took advantage of the previous empire's weakness during the instability caused by the war against the Theoclasts and seized power. The other cultures under Ozumi's rule consider them tyrants who imagine themselves superior to their own race. They are technologically advanced thanks to a partnership with the Republic of New Medietas. The Ozumi Empire is ruled by an empress who apparently takes direct orders from her divine ancestor, Susa-tsu-Nushi-no-Mikoto. There are several noble clans and a warrior caste that is in decline due to the use of firearms. There are still a few noble clans from other cultures who swore allegiance to Ozumi and were allowed to rule their ancestral lands. The "Wild Renshi" or "Barbarian Renshi" live outside of the Ozumi Empire's administration, mostly on the tundra and arctic climates of the far southern portion of the continent. They are mostly hunters, reindeer herders, and fishermen. They wear animal skins, live in tribes, and are very resistant to the cold (based on Inuit and Chukotko-Kamchatkan cultures)
their warrior class (akin to the samurai) is in decline due to the widespread use of firearms, thus many warrior clans founded conglomerates and began hiring commoners to work in fields such as metal processing, textiles, weapon fabrication, mass production of arcane goods etc. "Archaic" practices, such as martial arts, archery, and swordfighting are preserved due to their cultural value and people in the military are still trained for them
They have vast natural reserves that their national deity itself deemed sacred so that the nation doesn't lose its natural beauty. That's why most of the Ozumi factories and facilities are located in the mainland on lands traditionally inhabited by the Shun Renshi

Humans
The humans are the descendants of the humans who fled the Theoclasm on Pectus. They managed to obtain some examples of Theoclast technology during the war and, after reverse engineering, drastically developed their weapons, tools and architecture.
The Republic of New Medietas is an example of industrial advancement on the continent. Their society combines coal- and steam-powered machines with magical items.
The streets of the largest cities are teeming with citizens amid the rhythmic bustle of machines and the smoke of factories. The citizens of Nova Medietas boast an unwavering work ethic, where labor and industry reign supreme. A resolute commitment to capitalism fuels innovation and competition, driving the relentless pursuit of wealth and economic dominance.
Although Nova Medietas does not have a formal clan system, a select group of influential noble houses wield considerable power, guiding the nation's policies and future. These houses are closely linked to prosperous industrial conglomerates.
At the forefront of technological progress, the republic is a pioneer in the development of complex automatons and goelms and advanced machinery. Inventors and engineers drive notable advances, positioning the country as an industrial and technological powerhouse.
The Republic of New Medietas strategically allies itself with neighboring powers. They maintain a robust partnership with the Sulcaic Empire, reinforcing mutual interests and security. Likewise, friendly relations with the Ozumi Empire promote trade and technological collaboration.

Sulkai
Since they originated from Yuandi, the logistics of returning most of the Sulkai population from Pectus were simpler. Their empire has remained stable for the ~500 years since the Theoclasm took place. They appreciate refined food and items and place great importance on money and nobility. A good portion of the sulkai settlers in Pectus were merchants. As a general rule, they are gentle, delicate and sometimes passively aggressive. Their society and technology used to be more sophisticated than Pectus's until the humans made incredible advances. Their ship models are still the most used to navigate what little ocean that was left around Yuandi.
Their society is loosely divided into castes, but an individual can change social status relatively easily. There are the commoners, the merchants and artisans, the knights and soldiers, the burghers, the elite wizards and the nobility, with the imperial family at the top. Many of the sulkai who came to Pectus seeking to amass wealth returned to the Sulcaic Empire completely poor and in the condition of refugees.
Noble families are divided into clans with a semi-mythical ancestor being the founder of the house, a fundamental factor in legitimizing the relevance of a family. They have artifacts, which were supposedly forged by their ancestors. Their tales and stories often involve much more magic and the forces of nature. Superficially they look like pale humans with blue, green, or white hair and blue, green, or grey eyes, but their bodies function in quite different ways. Their longevity is greater, as is the time between childhood and maturity (a 30-year-old sulkai is considered a teenager). Their bodies are lighter and metabolic processes seem to affect their bodies much more, for example it takes much less time for a sulkai to get drunk or for a medicine to take effect. In the rare cases where they interbreed with humanoid races, the resulting progeny are always born sulkai. The incidence of aptitude for magic is extremely high, with 4 out of 5 having the potential. Their susceptibility to cold iron stems from the fact that they are descendants of the same ancestral population that originated the humans and eniyan of Pectus, who then interbred with faeries when they landed from the lost continent in the north of the world.
While the nobility holds great importance, heads of banks and commercial enterprises, each with a personal army, and each locked in a constant struggle against all the others, hold great relevance and economic power. They have enough capital to resolve any foreign diplomatic quandaries with a well-placed sum of money or threat of withdrawal from trade. Thus, many conflicts in other nations were resolved by the economic influence of certain organizations and companies.
Their religion differs drastically from the Church of YHVH. It is based on semi-mythical ancestor worship, who fulfill a similar role to saints. The existence of gods is recognized, but generally relegated to a secondary role, even if the Theoclasm made them inhabit the Barrier. Their fairy ancestors, or nature spirits, are worshiped instead.
They are considered to be more sophisticated and superior to other races, sometimes attracting the hatred of some individuals. They get along especially well with the humans, whom they consider their allies for having granted the Colony of Levantia to the Sulcaic Empire. With the Theoclasm, it was the sulkai's turn to cede territory to their allies. Their aptitude for trade is always welcome in the farthest reaches, and even tribal chiefs seek out the sulkai for business.
As mentioned earlier, it has been confirmed that sulkai descended from the union of proto-humans with fairies, or nature spirits. Namely naiads and haliads (water spirits), epigeia and dryads (nature spirits), aureads and boreads (wind spirits).

Anglo-Elves
Elves and Weisslander humans, after fleeing Pectus during the Theoclasm, unexpectedly found themselves sharing the same land west of the continent of Yuandi. Despite the mutual dislike between both races, they ended up mixing, resulting in the hybrid race known today as the Anglo-Elves. Even before the assimilation between both races, it was noted that children of elf-human couples always resulted in an appearance almost identical to that of humans, without the golden skin, pointed ears and light hair that elves prized. Strangely, the fruits of such unions were always born with red, orange or pinkish hair and elven eye colours (blue, green, golden).
Despite the mixing of these two races, there is still an elite of pure elves who govern the nation in a not so explicit way. Culturally, the Anglo-Elves are a fusion of elven and weisslander cultures, with a simultaneous focus on battles and intellectualism, on physical combat and magical combat, among other aspects. There are also a significant number of dark-skinned Anglo-Elves descended from the eniyan of Pectus.
Magic is a revered aspect of society, guided by guilds of wizards who educate potential wizards. Approximately half of Anglo-elves show potential for magic, with only a few becoming accomplished wizards.
The Anglo-Elves practice a syncretic faith that has characteristics of the faith of YHVH, the ancestor worship practiced by the Elves, and the tribal polytheism of the Weisslanders. Clans can trace their lineages to specific individuals who embarked on the journey fleeing the continent of Pectus. While ancestor worship is typically done in family shrines at home, the worship of YHVH is done in public temples.
The Anglo-Elves have long been at war with the Hazrun over territorial claims to an island to the west of both nations. This island, called Haséaleen by the Anglo-Elves and Haşarin by the Hazrun, has one of five pillars that maintain a protective barrier around the continent. The Anglo-Elves already have one of the towers, the Red Pillar, in their territory and want the Black Pillar, stating that Hazrun cannot be trusted to possess it.

Mustalf
Pectus’ “accursed race” again survives a great cataclysm and finds itself destined to roam another continent without its own land or nation. Unlike the ancient Dark Elves, the Mustalf (In Elvish: Must = Dark; Alf = Elf) no longer live only in underground shelters, currently choosing to live as nomadic traders who roam the nations buying and selling exotic goods. They have a few autonomous territories in Yuandi, and a number of mustalf live in the territory of the Followers of Ma’at. They are considered a cursed race by the elves. Thousands of years ago, the “Bloodstained Emperor” murdered the other three members of the Quadrumvirate and fled from the Sonne Insel archipelago to Pectus’ mainland with thousands of followers, who were later cursed by an unknown deity or altered by a powerful relic of the elves. The Alveglaan elves symbolically interpret the darkening of traitors as the mark of their unforgivable crime. Everyone is expected to work for the good of society, including children, the elderly and women. The Mustalf are trained from childhood to perform certain tasks or jobs and continue to contribute until they are unable to in some way. Their ears are movable and expressive, just like an elf’s. They have no body and facial hair (except eyebrows and eyelashes), which they consider a sign of barbarity. Short hair is socially accepted, both in men and women, but it is seen as a sign of youthfulness and immaturity. Probably as a result of their ancestors living underground, their hearing is sharper and their eyes are sensitive to light. The Mustalf have a strong sense of community and place a high value on loyalty and solidarity with their own kind. They have a tendency to put the needs of the community above the needs of the individual. Many of them consider it essential to learn at least one foreign language, to play at least one instrument, and to know at least one trade, since most of their livelihood depends on trading with different races.

Hazrun
One of the races native to Yuandi and the third most numerous. The hazrun were dominated for centuries by the Shun Dynasty. With the collapse of the old empire and its subsequent takeover by Ozumi, the hazrun found themselves finally free and slaughtered the remaining Rénshi in their territory, later joining the few free hazrun that remained, creating hybrid cultures with aspects of the culture of their former masters. To prevent another invasion and the enslavement of their people, the Hazrun militarized and today have large armies with highly efficient units, the result of their domestication of draconic species, such as drakes, wyverns, sauroids and avioserps. Many have returned to their old ways of life as reindeer herders, hunters and fishermen to forget their hateful past under another race's rule.
Their nation, known as the United Hordes of Jirkaeriya, is ruled by a Soho (Hazrunic: leader, ruler, king), who must be of "divine ancestry". In case the next leader is not elected peacefully, pretenders can unify the cultures/tribes. The current Hazrun nation is the result of the conquest of Tazkiairga and his wife Huzur, who fought against Tazkiairga's siblings to unify the Hazrun race.
Hazrun culture is diverse, with multiple "peoples" within the same nation. The biggest ones are Berihazrun (“Plain Hazrun”), Keiozhazrun (“River Hazrun”) and Damohazrun (“Mountain Hazrun”). Generally, women have short hair, letting it grow only after marriage, while the opposite occurs with men, who may also cut their hair during military service as a symbol of their “marriage to the nation”. Like the ancient elves, they have no body or facial hair. Women walk with midriff-revealing clothes while single to indicate they are available, but cover them up once they get boyfriends or husbands. The Hazrun wear earrings, necklaces, and body paint with various symbols that other races do not understand. Wars and battles are mostly fought only by men, as hazrun women are naturally physically smaller and weaker. Some hordes have women who specialize in magic and assassination.
The most peculiar feature of the hazrun is certainly the presence of horns, which are highly prized in all their cultures. They also have four fingers on each hand and foot, harder nails, and sharper fangs. Individuals with branched horns like those of a deer, called Adarkahazrun ("Branched Horn"), make up the "upper caste" of the hazrun, i.e., clan chiefs, rulers, and military leaders. The hazrun see hornless races as unworthy or dishonorable. They are not able to breed with other races, so it is more accurate to refer to them as another species. It is noted that they are very resistant to alcohol and cannot feel spicy tastes very well.

Usagizok
They have a strong sense of balance and agility, allowing them to move quickly and gracefully through the natural landscapes. Usagizok developed unique cultural practices based on their connection to nature. They have a ritual for thanking the plants and animals they rely on for sustenance and have developed a system of using natural resources sustainably. Their enhanced hearing also plays a role in their culture. They have developed a form of communication in a frequency that only members of their own species can hear.
The Usagizok were enslaved by the Shun Dynasty for being exotic and were even seen as pets by some. This led to tensions between the two races even after the fall of the dynasty. The Usagizok have long ears like rabbits or hares, a fur-covered body, resistant claws for digging and very strong leg muscles that enable them to jump higher and farther away than the other races. Their incisors are bigger and stronger due to their mostly vegetarian diet which consists mostly of root vegetables, leaves, and fruits. Some of them have short tails very similar to a rabbit’s. In terms of their current situation, the Usagizok are struggling to find their place in the world since being freed from slavery. They have difficulty integrating into other societies and prefer isolating themselves and live a more nomadic lifestyle in their partially underground warrens.
As a result of their enslavement, Usagizok are usually not taken seriously by other races. They may have difficulty finding work or housing outside of their own communities, and may face discrimination or violence. Despite this, the Usagizok have managed to carve out their own niche in society. They are skilled at jobs that require agility, such as acrobatics or hunting, and have developed a reputation as skilled scouts, mercenaries, assassins, and spies due to their heightened senses and physical abilities. Many Usagizok have withdrawn from the larger world and created their own isolated communities, hidden away in forests or other remote areas. These communities are wary of outsiders and have their own unique customs and traditions. The Usagizok are matriarchal; a warren is mostly composed of related members descended from the same maternal ancestor. They are very fertile. A pregnancy lasts for only 4 months and the offspring, often born as quadruplets or triplets, reach childhood in 2 years and sexual maturity in 10. The females in the warren take turns nursing the newborns while the males cultivate plants or go out to trade, forage or hunt. To avoid inbreeding, they have a tradition of visiting other warrens to find suitable spouses. A matriarch can have multiple husbands. Like the Hazrun, they cannot interbreed with other races
Usagizok are grappling with their own internal divisions and conflicts between different tribes and factions. This is related both to differences in religious or cultural practices and by more pragmatic concerns such as access to resources or disputes over leadership.

in 150 words at most please write me a professional, eloquent and gramatically impressive conclusion for the following question: “In your opinion, should students have unlimited access to these AI systems (e.g., Chat GPT, Claude 2, Bard etc.)? Please draw on personal examples as well as academic references to support your answer.” Given that this is the answer I’ve conjured up for the question: “Technological innovation has thoroughly permeated countless facet of our existence, with the domain of education being no exception. In the midst of this exponentially evolving modernity of technological advancements, the dawn of generative artificial intelligence systems, have inaugurated a global debate regarding their integration and accessibility within education. Despite these avant-garde programmes, furnished with their prodigious yet arguably latent capacity to assimilate, generate, and customise content, bestowing upon students unparalleled opportunities for knowledge attainment and intellectual expansion; a cavalcade of potential pitfalls, ethical quandaries and pedagogical challenges that necessitate exhaustive academic scrutiny emerge. As we stand on the precipice of a new educational epoch, the widespread question emerges: Should students be granted boundless access to these systems? I contend that allowing students unfettered access to advanced AI tools could, contrary to expectations, impede educational progress and yield detrimental effects due to underlying ethical, scholastic, and developmental concerns. The quintessential contention in opposition to bestowing upon students unfettered access is firmly rooted in the principles aligned with academic integrity and the threat artificial intelligence constitutes to corroding any sense of it. Artificial intelligence systems, given their capabilities for content generation (contextually assignments/ essays etc.), could potentially facilitate an environment where original thought is negated yet supplanted by artificial intelligence generated responses, thereby calling into question the authenticity of ‘student- composed’ workings. (McCabe, et al., 2012) expound on the value of academic honesty as a cornerstone of educational institutions and learning processes whilst emphasising the principle that one’s work should be the product of one’s own understanding- an assertation of which I am wholly in accord with. Permitting students to the inexhaustible access of artificial intelligence programmes could undermine this tenet, as students may fabricate a grave dependence on generated material, thus impeding the cultivation of critical thinking and analytical abilities concurrently with invalidating any form of assessment process, which in theory is conceived to evaluate individual student learning and achievement (Newton, 2016). Such a dependency may involuntarily encourage a culture of lethargy and academic dishonesty (a culture of which I have personally bear witnessed where students would doubt and voluntarily omit their own academic facilities for insubstantial recapitulated artificially generated work), where plagiarism, not of texts, but ideas is conventional- subconsciously shifting the role of a student as an active learner to that of a passive regurgitator of generative artificial intelligence generated output; contributing to the devaluation of the educational process (Hughs & McCabe, 2006). Cognitive atrophy is a dormant threat in the scenario when enabling students to unlimited access to artificial intelligence generative programmes. Mechanisms of which may jeopardize and stifle the development of critical thinking and deep learning in students- two cornerstone objectives of education. Should students become overly dependent on artificial intelligence- this disproportionate dependence is also inversely proportional to compromising one’s prowess of maintaining prolonged concentration and introspective thought; there also lies a danger of fostering an ‘automation complacency’, a phenomenon whereby they (the students in question) subconsciously begin placing excessive trust in automated support, thereby attenuating their analytical rigor (Carr, 2011; Carr, 2014). To further accentuate this point, a study by (Sparrow, et al., 2011) found that people are less likely to retain information that is uncomplicatedly procurable online, suggesting that the ubiquitous nature of artificial intelligence could similarly affect memory and learning. Whilst being a computer science undergraduate at Cardiff Metropolitan University, we were tasked with devising and coding an optimised time complexity sorting algorithm. Delving into the intricacies of various sorting techniques, from bubble sort to selection sort to quicksort, this required substantial mental exertion and iteration. Though had we been given unrestricted access to the readily accessible assortment of modes of generative artificial intelligence, the looming temptation to simply generate the code would certainly have circumvented the valuable intellectual process of comparing efficiencies and leveraging algorithmic thinking. In accordance with (Bower & Sturman, 2015), educational technologies should be tools for the enhancement of learning, not substitutions for cognitive processes which in this example easily could have been the case. Data privacy/ security is another compelling argument against unbridled access to artificial intelligence systems. All platforms, whilst ostensibly altruistic in provisioning ‘free services’, operate within the data economy where user interactions are a commodity and gathered on an incomprehensible scale to tailor their outputs (Zuboff, 2019). Artificial intelligence platforms, necessitating an extensive trove of data in order to function optimally, not only raise concerns over data ownership and vulnerability but also emphasise that, as primary users, the student demographic inadvertently generates a considerable amount of ‘lucrative’ and sensitive personal data susceptible to commercial exploitation, security infringements, and identity theft (Solove, 2013; Zuboff, 2019). Rebuttals such as the following aforementioned render the notion of unconstrained access fundamentally at odds with, whilst simultaneously juxtaposing the ‘Privacy by Design’ (≅ data protection through technology design) principle (Cavoukian, 2009). This issue is further entangled by the nuances of informed consent; the more youthful student base may not possess the requisite depth of comprehending to providing informed consent pertaining to the use of their data whether it be for machine learning processes or not, in theory allowing artificial intelligence systems to capitalise on their naivety and erode personal autonomy in a realm where the sanctity of consent ought to be paramount (Roseenblat, et al., 2014). On the subject of data privacy/ security, I myself as someone who personally is averse to equipping students with unimpeded artificial intelligence access, reminisces on the reprehensible case of Facebook and the Cambridge Analytica scandals which servers as a stark reminder of the perils associated with vast data assemblages being mismanaged (Chadwalladr & Graham-Harrison, 2018).”

Economic Standpoint and Profit Adequacy Amid Monopolistic Leverage

From an economic standpoint, the scrutiny of Mylan’s monopoly over the EpiPen market must consider profitability and the market mechanisms that influenced its pricing strategies. Mylan’s substantial growth over the decades, paired with its 2007 EpiPen acquisition, marked the transition from a mission centered around affordable access to a more global and ambiguous commitment to setting new standards in healthcare. While the loftiness of its vision implies beneficence, the price escalation of the EpiPen raises the question of whether profit maximization overshadowed the company’s purported ethical compass.

Mylan’s monopolistic hold on the EpiPen market in the United States, facilitated to an extent by the regulatory environment of the FDA, became a source of immense profitability. The rejection of competitor products and the complexities of bringing a rival auto-injector to market cultivated an environment where Mylan’s pricing decisions faced little opposition. The case studies suggest that Mylan’s margins on the EpiPen were indeed substantial, contributing significantly to the company’s bottom line. Europe’s multiple producers of epinephrine auto-injectors stand in stark contrast to the American landscape, where Mylan enjoyed uncontested economic leverage—a gap that the FDA’s stringent approval process helped to preserve.

The interplay between Mylan’s monopoly and FDA regulatory action is critical. The hurdles faced by potential competitors, such as recall of competing products and rejections of entry bids by the FDA, highlight structural impediments to market competition. While the safety of the public is non-negotiable, the equivalence or adequacy of competing auto-injectors appeared to become secondary to the more pressing issue of accessibility and affordability, exacerbated by Mylan’s aggressive pricing.

Mylan’s use of tactics like ‘pay-for-delay’ and the questioning of its EpiPen school program’s ethics further underline the discrepancy between public service and self-interest. Political interventions to address the prospect of price gouging indicated an understanding that regulatory measures could serve as effective deterrents to economic exploitation. Proposals ranged from expedited FDA approvals for generic products to fundamental changes such as eliminating the prescription-only requirement for EpiPens—each with implications for competition and pricing.

Upon investigation, Mylan’s professed profit margins from the sales of EpiPens, as presented to the House Oversight and Reform Committee by CEO Heather Bresch, came under skepticism. Not only did law enforcement officials challenge the veracity of these figures, but subsequent disclosures revealed that Mylan had significantly understated its profit margins by including taxes at the statutory corporate tax rate, rather than the substantially lower rate they actually incurred. Further, the $465 million settlement for wrongly classifying EpiPen as a generic to dodge higher rebates to Medicaid exemplified a corporate maneuvering to retain high profitability at the expense of ethical practice and societal expectations.

Thus, in the context of Mylan’s history, mission, and vision, the surge in EpiPen’s price and the observed monopolistic dominance—which crowded out competition and led to public outcry—reflect a breach of both economic equity and the company’s purported ethical framework. The economic adequacy of Mylan’s pricing strategy, which raised profitability while arguably neglecting the affordability for those in dire need of EpiPens, stands at odds with the initial mission statement to “help people…gain access to affordable medicine.” The literature therefore suggests that from both an economic and ethical standpoint, Mylan’s pricing of the life-saving EpiPen was neither adequate nor justifiable, inciting valid controversy and regulatory action.

Natsuki: (sighs) “Yeah. It’s about my ex-boyfriend Lunagaron.”

Monika: “Oh, I didn’t know you had an ex-boyfriend. What happened between you two, Natsuki?”

Natsuki: “We recently broke up, and I can’t help but think about it constantly. It’s been really tough for me, especially since I told him about this…” (lifting up her shirt to reveal her belly) “…burden.”

Monika: (surprised) “Oh… Natsuki, I didn’t expect this. Are you… are you saying you’re pregnant?”

Natsuki: (nods, her voice trembling) “Yeah…7 months along now. I didn’t plan for any of this. We were both supposed to be using protection, but something went wrong.”

Monika: “I’m really sorry to hear that, Natsuki. That must be incredibly difficult for you. Have you talked to Lunagaron about it? How did he react?”

Natsuki: “He was shocked at first, just like me. We both never anticipated this happening. But when I entered my second trimester, he started acting distant and eventually broke up with me. He said he wasn’t ready for the responsibility of being a father, and he didn’t want it to affect his future plans.”

Monika: “I can’t imagine how heartbreaking that must have been for you, Natsuki. It’s never easy going through something like this, especially without the support of the person you thought would be by your side. Do you have anyone else you can turn to for support?”

Natsuki: “Not really… My friends are great, but they don’t understand what I’m going through. And my parents… they would be devastated if they found out. I just feel so alone.”

Monika: “I’m really sorry to hear that, Natsuki. You shouldn’t have to go through this alone. Is there anyone you can trust, maybe a counselor or a teacher, who could help you deal with everything?”

Natsuki: “I’ve thought about it, but I’m afraid of what people will think. I don’t want to be judged or treated differently because of this. I just want to find a way to handle it on my own.”

Monika: “It’s completely understandable to feel that way, but remember that reaching out for support doesn’t make you weak or any less capable. Sometimes, having someone to lean on can make a world of difference. They can offer guidance, advice, and just be there to listen when you need to talk.”

Natsuki: “I… I guess you’re right. It’s just hard to admit that I can’t handle everything on my own. But I’ll think about it. Maybe talking to someone would actually help.”

Monika: “That’s a good first step, Natsuki. Remember, you don’t have to carry this burden alone. We’re here for you too, in the literature club. If you ever need someone to talk to or lend a listening ear, please don’t hesitate to reach out.”

Natsuki: (smiling faintly) “Thank you, Monika. I really appreciate that. It means a lot to me.”

Monika: “Of course, Natsuki. We’re a team here, and we’re here to support each other through the good times and the difficult ones. We’ll get through this together.”

Natsuki: (looking at her belly) “Oh!”

(Startled, Natsuki puts her hand on her belly.)

Monika: “Is everything okay, Natsuki?”

Natsuki: (blushing) “Yeah, sorry. It’s just that my little girl kicked. I think I’ll name her Sakura. It’s a constant reminder of what I’m going through.”

Monika: “That’s a beautiful name, Natsuki. Sakura signifies strength and beauty, just like you. She’s lucky to have such a strong and caring mother like you.”

Natsuki: (smiling) “Thank you, Monika. That means a lot to me. I want to do my best for her, even in this difficult situation.”

Monika: “I have no doubt that you will, Natsuki. And remember, you don’t have to face this alone. We’re here for you, both as friends and as part of the literature club.”

Natsuki: “I really appreciate that, Monika. It means a lot to have your support.” (feeling another kick) “Ah!! Alright, Sakura, I get it. You’re excited to meet everyone too.” (laughs)

Monika: (laughs) “Looks like Sakura is already eager to make her presence known.”

Natsuki: “Yeah, she definitely has a lot of energy. I just hope I can keep up with her once she’s here.”

Monika: “I have no doubt that you’ll be an amazing mother, Natsuki. You have so much love and care to give. And Sakura is lucky to have you.”

# Define the neural network model.
class RNNModel(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, input_size, hidden_sizes, layer_types):
        super(RNNModel, self).__init__()
        self.layers = nn.ModuleList()
        for i, layer_type in enumerate(layer_types):
            input_dim = input_size if i == 0 else hidden_sizes[i - 1]
            if layer_type == 'LSTM':
                self.layers.append(nn.LSTM(input_dim, hidden_sizes[i], batch_first=True))
            elif layer_type == 'GRU':
                self.layers.append(nn.GRU(input_dim, hidden_sizes[i], batch_first=True))
            elif layer_type == 'Transformer':
                transformer_layer = nn.TransformerEncoderLayer(d_model=input_dim, nhead=1)
                self.layers.append(nn.TransformerEncoder(transformer_layer, num_layers=1))
            else:
                raise ValueError(f"Unrecognized layer type: {layer_type}")

    def forward(self, x):
        for layer in self.layers:
            if isinstance(layer, nn.TransformerEncoder):
                x = layer(x)
            else:
                x, _ = layer(x)
        return x

    def train_model(self, model, train_data_loader):
        if model is None:
          self.showMessage("Error", "Model not defined.")
          return
 
        num_epochs = self.num_epochs_spinbox.value()
        criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
        optimizer = optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=0.001)

        model.train()
        for epoch in range(num_epochs):
           running_loss = 0.0
           for i, batch in enumerate(train_data_loader):
            for batch in train_data_loader:
                inputs, labels = batch
                
                optimizer.zero_grad()
                outputs = model(inputs)
                loss = criterion(outputs, labels)
                loss.backward()
                optimizer.step()
            
        running_loss += loss.item()
        if i % 100 == 99:  # print every 100 mini-batches
                   print(f"Batch {i + 1}, Loss: {running_loss / 100}")
                   running_loss = 0.0

Предприимчивость (от англ. “entrepreneurial”) — это качество личности, присущее людям, которые склонны брать на себя риск, начинать и управлять бизнесом или другими видами деятельности. Это понятие ассоциируется с инициативностью, инновационностью, творческим подходом к решению проблем, способностью видеть возможности там, где другие их не видят, и готовностью к действиям.

Люди, обладающие качеством предприимчивости, часто характеризуются следующими чертами:

- Инициативность: они активно ищут новые возможности и готовы к действию, не ожидая, пока кто-то другой предпримет первый шаг.
- Решимость: они настойчивы и целеустремленны в достижении своих целей.
- Толерантность к риску: хотя они осторожно взвешивают риски, они готовы идти на них ради потенциальной прибыли или успешного развития своих проектов.
- Инновационность: они постоянно ищут новые идеи и способы улучшения чего-либо, не боятся экспериментировать.
- Гибкость: они способны быстро адаптироваться к изменяющимся условиям и обстоятельствам.
- Самомотивация: они энергичны и умеют поддерживать высокий уровень мотивации, даже сталкиваясь с трудностями или сопротивлением.

Document 4.Moins de gaz à effet de serre, mais un bilan énergétique mitigéGlobalement, la combustion des biocarburant produit moins de gaz à effet de serre (GES) que les énergies fossiles comme le gasoilou l’essence: entre 24% et 91% de GES en moins. En effet, comme les énergies fossiles, la combustion des biocarburants dégage du dioxyde de carbone (ou CO2, l’un des gaz à effet de serre responsables du réchauffement climatique), mais celle-ci est compensée, en partie du moins, par le CO2 qui avait été absorbé par les plantes lors de leur croissance ce qui n’est pas le cas du pétrole ou du charbon.Cependant, la production d’agro-carburants implique l’utilisation d’engrais et de pesticideschimiques (et donc dérivés du pétrole…), de carburant pour faire fonctionner le matériel agricole, de l’énergie pour le fonctionnement des usines productrices de biocarburants, et du carburant (ou de l’électricité) pour le transport des matières premières agricoles. Si l’on prend en compte toutes ces étapes le bilan est nettement moins satisfaisant et dans certains cas, l’émission de GES est plus importanteavec lesbio-carburants qu’avec les énergies fossiles. Indépendamment du bilan des gaz à effet de serrela biomasse présente quelques inconvénientspour l’instant non résolus :-Le détournement de millions d’hectares arables sensées nourrir la population seraient mis au profil des biocarburants.-Une déforestation intense au Brésil et en Asie du Sud qui sont les principaux producteurs de biocarburant.On sait que chaque jour environ 200 km2 de forêtsont détruites, ce qui fait environ 130 000 à 150 000 km2 de forêts rasées chaque année.-Risque d’épuisement des réserves d’eau car les cultures céréalières étant à l’origine des biocarburants sont gourmands en eau.-La culture à très grande échelle de la betterave ou du maïs nécessiterait de nombreux engrais chimiques dégageant des gaz à effet de serre comme par exemple le protoxyde d’azote, 296 plus polluants que le CO2.Les biocarburants sont donc une solution nouvelle, mais l’idéal serait de développer une énergie à la foisrenouvelable et non-polluante.

Palma 2018 It is our responsibility to respond to
the current and future needs of society and we must know how to face this
challenge, combining the promotion
of social housing based on its social
purpose and environmental awareness. When it comes to both social and
environmental sustainability, we think
and take action with social housing
developments that involve techniques
that generate, both in their construction and maintenance, lower amounts
of CO2
and waste, whilst at the same
time, working to promote the use of
sustainable power.
This book explains the origins and development of this flagship project to
address efficient construction in our
islands: LIFE+ 2012, an initiative recognised by the European Union and that
came to fruition through the construction of 14 social housing units in Sant
Ferran, Formentera.
This project has made it possible to
link our natural resources to the cultural tradition of Formentera. A good example is the use of dry Posidonia
oceanica as a construction material,
as was the traditional method. Harnessing a waste product that is plentiful and native to Formentera, using its
properties as thermal insulation and
thus avoiding having to use materials
that do not exist in our islands provides a new approach to both public
and private construction.
Enhancing our cultural tradition whilst
promoting greater energy efficiency
and the use of ecological technologies increases the competitiveness
of our production systems and helps
to maintain and care for our natural
resources. This is the path that we
should be taking.
I would like to publicly acknowledge
everybody who has worked both persistently and decidedly to convert the Balearic Islands into a reference point in
the Mediterranean in the field of bio architecture. Furthermore, I would like to
highlight the role of our partners in this
initiative who, with the utmost in professionalism, have catalysed an approach
that helps to ensure that public buildings are nearly zero-energy buildings.
Congratulations to everybody involved
in this project, which has been the result of a joint effort, full of hope, that is
truly innovative and pioneering.
Marc Pons i Pons

Similarly, progress towards a degree of self-sufficiency in resource consumption is one of the main
ways of reducing the so-called “ecological threats”, which are actually
threats to the social system46. It is

Within the 14 social housing units in Sant Ferran, Formentera, the spatial vision is approached with the dual aim of utilizing space efficiently while allowing flexibility for varied uses within each unit. The layout and design of the various unit types, scrutinized both in plan and section, reflect an ethos where the relationship between inhabitants and their environment is intimate and interactive. The variety among the units, from single-level apartments to duplex accommodations, answers to the diverse needs and lifestyles of future residents while keeping the density within check.

The design introspects density within the unit meticulously. Each space is crafted to serve multiple functions—a living room that seamlessly transforms into a workspace, bedrooms that cater to rest and study. Provisions have been made to accommodate studios or working spaces within or adjacent to the units, ensuring that the need for external commuting can be reduced, and sustainability and lifestyle balance are encouraged. 

The units have been organized to align with different daily activities and user groups. Areas designated for formal and informal purposes coexist harmoniously—a kitchen integrated into the living area promotes social interaction, while private quarters are reserved for tranquility and personal space. This functional overlay within the unit space not only combats the notion of traditional compartmentalization but also enables the inhabitants to customize their living experience.

Circulation within the units has been devised to offer alternative pathways, affording a sense of freedom and fluidity. This thoughtful arrangement stimulates a dwelling environment where the journey through a home is neither linear nor prescriptive but an explorative narrative.

The distinct unit types each propose a lifestyle vision—flexible and modern for the individual urban dweller, secure and communal for families, sociable yet private for the elderly. The residents are encouraged to inhabit spaces that resonate with their personal routines and cultural nuances, offering a canvas upon which life is not just lived but also felt and experienced. Hence, the spatial vision in the Sant Ferran housing project is not only about the tangibility of walls and floors but also about the intangibles of community, flexibility, and lifestyle.

Summarize it with citation...A sugarcane cooperative, also known as a sugarcane growers’ cooperative, is an organization or association formed by farmers who grow sugarcane. The purpose of these cooperatives is to collectively market and sell their sugarcane crops, negotiate prices, and purchase inputs like fertilizers and machinery at a bulk rate.

Sugarcane cooperatives can be found in many countries where sugarcane is a major agricultural crop, such as Brazil, India, Australia, and Thailand. These cooperatives typically operate under a cooperative structure, where each member has an equal voice and vote in the decision-making process.

The main advantages of sugarcane cooperatives are that they provide collective bargaining power for small-scale sugarcane farmers, enable cost-sharing for inputs, enhance access to credit, and promote knowledge sharing among members. By working together, farmers in a sugarcane cooperative can often negotiate better prices for their crops and secure a more stable income.

Additionally, sugarcane cooperatives often provide technical assistance and training to their members, helping them improve their farming practices, enhance productivity, and adopt sustainable agricultural methods.

Sugarcane cooperatives also play a significant role in the local economy, as they contribute to rural development and job creation. They often establish processing facilities, such as sugar mills or ethanol distilleries, which create employment opportunities and add value to the local sugarcane industry.

Overall, sugarcane cooperatives serve as a collective platform for sugarcane farmers to pool their resources and expertise, enabling them to improve their livelihoods while strengthening the sugarcane industry as a whole.

I would like to tell you about a country called the Grand Union of America, or GUA. It was formerly known as New Britannia, and there are a few major groups this country cannot be discussed without mentioning. First are the Pilgrims. Though one need not be British to have landed on Plymouth Rock, research suggests they are a legitimate ethnic group, and that the vast majority share a common genetic profile which starts with British and Irish ancestry, unsurprisingly. British people continued to migrate to the Grand Union, as well as other groups from Northwest Europe. Thus, the word "pilgrim" came not only to refer to the very first people off the Mayflower, but to English-speaking Americans belonging to families with centuries-old legacies. Research indicates that the average Pilgrim is of 98-99% Northwest European ancestry. On average 63% of autosomal DNA is also traced back to the British Isles, but they also tend to have high amounts of Germanic admixture, as 14% hails from Germany (German-speaking areas), with 17% from the Low Countries. 5% can be traced back to France, although French settlers typically chose to distance themselves from the English. This brings me to my next point.
Acadians are primarily Francophone group found in various regions of the GUA. As can be inferred, they make up a smaller group than Pilgrims. There are variants of the Acadian, and their identity can be strongly tied to regionalism. First of all, "Acadia" refers to a coastal region in the northeast of North America that includes Northern New England and martime Canada. This is where it all began, their Plymouth Rock. Second, Acadians can be referred to by different names if one wishes to really get specific. In the former Louisiana Territory, you will find "Cajuns." In Quebec, you will find Quebecois. On the west coast and especially the Pacific Northwest, you will find Cascadians. The Acadian population is estimated at 36-44 million strong.
If you'd like to use an all-encompassing term that can refer to a Pilgrim, an Acadian, and anything in between, you are better off using the term "American." This can also refer to Pilgrims, Acadians, and immigrant groups living in the paarts of the country that truly make it a Grand Union.
As far as basic information goes, its capital is Philadelphia. This is part of the state of Galloway (named after Joseph Galloway, a major figure in the passage of the Reconciliation Acts of 1768). Galloway obviously includes Pennsylvania but also includes some of the other core colonies, some of the oldest such as Virginia, Maryland, Delaware, New Jersey, and New York. Other foundational states include New England (MA, CT, RI, VT, NH, ME), the Canadian Maritimes, Ontario, Quebec, and Carolina (NC and SC.). Each state is important, but key newer ones include Florida (Florida and Cuba) Austin (Texas, OK, KS, WY, UT, AZ), Dixie (TN, AK, LA, MS, AL, GA), Huron (MI, WI, MN, IA, IL, IN, OH,MS, KY.), Serena (CA, NV, OR, WA), and Montalucio (ID, MT, CO, ND, SD, NE.) Central Britannia, which is pretty much the core of the entire cross-continental country, is predominantly European, and they account for 81% of the population, although Hispanics, Africans, and Filipinos also live in there. However because of past trends many of these groups do have significant European admixture and some with very high admixture can look indistinguishable from Europeans. In this timeline, slavery was abolished in 1814, so it has fewer Africans, as they account for 2.5% of the population of the CCB. Additionally, half repatriated to Liberia (Note: In this scenario, Liberia has thrived, and with American guidance and investment it became comparable to South Africa.) The national currency of is the US Dollar ($).

Palma 2018 It is our responsibility to respond to
the current and future needs of society and we must know how to face this
challenge, combining the promotion
of social housing based on its social
purpose and environmental awareness. When it comes to both social and
environmental sustainability, we think
and take action with social housing
developments that involve techniques
that generate, both in their construction and maintenance, lower amounts
of CO2
and waste, whilst at the same
time, working to promote the use of
sustainable power.
This book explains the origins and development of this flagship project to
address efficient construction in our
islands: LIFE+ 2012, an initiative recognised by the European Union and that
came to fruition through the construction of 14 social housing units in Sant
Ferran, Formentera.
This project has made it possible to
link our natural resources to the cultural tradition of Formentera. A good example is the use of dry Posidonia
oceanica as a construction material,
as was the traditional method. Harnessing a waste product that is plentiful and native to Formentera, using its
properties as thermal insulation and
thus avoiding having to use materials
that do not exist in our islands provides a new approach to both public
and private construction.
Enhancing our cultural tradition whilst
promoting greater energy efficiency
and the use of ecological technologies increases the competitiveness
of our production systems and helps
to maintain and care for our natural
resources. This is the path that we
should be taking.
I would like to publicly acknowledge
everybody who has worked both persistently and decidedly to convert the Balearic Islands into a reference point in
the Mediterranean in the field of bio architecture. Furthermore, I would like to
highlight the role of our partners in this
initiative who, with the utmost in professionalism, have catalysed an approach
that helps to ensure that public buildings are nearly zero-energy buildings.
Congratulations to everybody involved
in this project, which has been the result of a joint effort, full of hope, that is
truly innovative and pioneering.

structures.

The Sant Ferran housing project, a crystallization of the LIFE Reusing Posidonia initiative, exhibits an integrative programmatic vision that weaves together communal living with individual privacy. The integration of uses within the plan has crafted a multifaceted environment that supports various aspects of daily life. The architectural articulation harmonizes residential spaces with communal amenities, which include shared courtyards that act as extended living areas, fostering interaction and community activities. An interplay of open and enclosed spaces enables residents to enjoy the mild Mediterranean climate, while also providing options for seclusion.

The arrangement of these communal realms within the complex is thoughtful and purposeful. Positioned centrally, these shared spaces serve as the heart of the complex, encouraging a sense of belonging and community. The positioning of playgrounds, seating areas and shared gardens captures the essence of collective living, extending the domestic sphere beyond the walls of individual units.

The circulation is both a literal and figurative backbone of the complex, eschewing lengthy corridors for direct external access from the street for the ground-level units, and optimizing vertical circulation cores to serve the elevated duplexes. This elimination of superfluous passageways contributes to the project’s low-density feeling, despite its collective housing typology.

Addressing the density in terms of apartment variety, the design delivers a tapestry of units that cater to a range of inhabitants, from single residents to families. Each is thoughtfully placed to maximize natural resources and communal connectivity. There is a deliberate cohesion within clusters of units, creating sub-communities that are interlinked, yet possess their individual character when viewed in elevation. The visual variance mitigates potential monotony, an often-cited critique of collective housing, infusing an architectural vibrancy while adhering to the environmental ethos of IBAVI’s undertaking.

In totality, the Sant Ferran development’s programmatic principles represent an evolutionary step in addressing the challenges of density, community, and ecological integration. The design iterates a template conducive to social interaction within the bounds of sustainable living, presenting a paradigm influential to future design considerations at the periphery of urban contexts.

class VideoCaptureAsync:
    def init(self, source=0):
        self.cap = cv2.VideoCapture(source)
        self.q = Queue(maxsize=1)
        self.running = False

    def start(self):
        self.running = True
        self.thread = Thread(target=self.update, args=())
        self.thread.start()
        return self

    def update(self):
        while self.running:
            ret, frame = self.cap.read()
            if not ret:
                self.running = False
                break
            if not self.q.full():

                    try:
                        # Remove the previous frame
                        self.q.get_nowait()
                    except Queue.Empty:
                        pass
                self.q.put(frame)

    def read(self):
        return self.q.get()

    def stop(self):
        self.running = False
        self.thread.join()
        self.cap.release()

    def exit(self, exc_type, exc_value, traceback):
        self.cap.release()

def object_detection_camera_with_roi(source, weights=‘yolov5s.pt’, conf_thres=0.25, person_class_id=0):
    # Load the YOLOv5 model
    model = YOLOv5(weights, autoshape=True)
    model.conf = conf_thres
    model.classes = [person_class_id]  # only detect person class
    model.eval()

    source.start()
    try:
        with torch.no_grad():
            while True:
                frame = source.read()
                
                # Define ROI size and position (centered)
                h, w = frame.shape[:2]
                roi_size = min(w, h) // 3
                x1, y1 = w // 2 - roi_size // 2, h // 2 - roi_size // 2
                x2, y2 = x1 + roi_size, y1 + roi_size
                
                # Extract the ROI from the frame
                roi = frame[y1:y2, x1:x2]
                
                # Inference on the ROI
                results = model(roi)
                
                # Draw the ROI rectangle on the original frame
                cv2.rectangle(frame, (x1, y1), (x2, y2), (255, 0, 0), 2)
                
                # Count the number of people detected
                people_count = 0
                
                # Extract detections
                for *xyxy, conf, cls in results.xyxy[0]:
                    # Rescale coordinates to the original frame
                    xyxy = (torch.tensor(xyxy).view(1, 4) * torch.tensor([w / roi_size, h / roi_size, w / roi_size, h / roi_size])).view(-1).tolist()
                    x1_box, y1_box, x2_box, y2_box = [int(coord) for coord in xyxy]
                    x1_box += x1
                    y1_box += y1
                    x2_box += x1
                    y2_box += y1
                    
                    # Increment people count and draw bounding boxes and labels on the original frame
                    if conf > conf_thres:
                        people_count += 1
                        label = f’Person {conf:.2f}‘
                        cv2.rectangle(frame, (x1_box, y1_box), (x2_box, y2_box), (0, 255, 0), 2)
                        cv2.putText(frame, label, (x1_box, y1_box - 10), cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX, 0.5, (0, 255, 0), 2)
                
                # Display the number of people detected

                cv2.imshow(‘YOLOv5 Object Detection with ROI - Camera’, frame)

                # Break loop with ‘q’
                if cv2.waitKey(1) == ord(‘q’):

Text: During the Tang (618–906) and Song (960–1279) Dynasties, China was one of the most technologically advanced civilizations in the world. Innovation in art, science, philosophy, and technology gave the people in these societies an understanding of the world around them that other civilizations and even later dynasties in China would not accomplish for hundreds of years. 

Like other golden ages in history, the Tang and Song Dynasties unified the region, created a strong central government, and ruled over a time of peace that was reinforced by the government’s actions. The Tang expanded China’s territories and influence to include Korea and Vietnam, as well as portions of northeast, central, and southeast Asia. 

The peace that the Tang and Song governments created encouraged trade throughout the empire and abroad through the Silk Roads. Chinese cities during the Tang and Song dynasties became prosperous cultural centers of an international age where religious, academic, and artistic life and cultural exchange flourished. Scholars and merchants from as far as Persia and India came to Tang China to participate in its golden age. 

While the government was strong, it was not oppressive. Some became very rich, but the Tang rulers redistributed land to give the less fortunate an opportunity to grow in wealth. In addition this was a time when education and achievement were rewarded and women attained a higher status in the government and more freedom than they had in previous dynasties.

Understanding the differentiation between fixed and variable costs is essential for gaining insight into a company's complete cost framework, as both total costs and variable costs contribute to forming a comprehensive view of the business's financial landscape. This comprehension is crucial for making informed assessments about the company's spending (Weygandt et al., 2020). 
Such expenditures as rent, insurance, and wages are referred to as fixed costs since output volume does not affect them. 
Variable costs, such as the price of materials and labor, are expenditures whose amounts vary depending on the output volume.

Pop was originally launched on 29 May 2003 by Chart Show Channels (CSC) Media Group as Toons&Tunes. Toons&Tunes was then later rebranded as its current name, Pop (formerly stylized as pop and POP!) in the following month.

In the channel's early years, links were presented by Rorry, a lime green dragon with a Scottish accent, who was animated live. He was accompanied by Purrdy, a dragon/cat hybrid who also appeared in the original Tricky programme on ITV1, it was sometimes followed by a programme known as "The Cheeky Monkey Show" which features the live links of the animated coloured monkeys known as "The Cheeky Monkeys," that was later known by appearing on its sister channel Tiny Pop until its retirement at the end of June 2009.
